Timing rules are shared by all languages: src/data/lines.schedule.json (T-011m, D-055) — this file has no schedule block. When the user picks new lines, Cowork adds them to every language at once. T-025 (D-058): 53 new lines s156–s208 (moments income:1m/1b/1t, session_hour, energy_near, training_half, release:2, release:3 and more lines for frequent moments), s124 removed, s057, s078, s082, s120 updated to economy v2.5. T-025b: 9 more lines s209–s217 from round 8 (any_purchase, pause). T-034 (D-074): Smith’s new friendly voice — no “meatbag”-style nicknames, only childish villainy. 79 lines use the variants the user chose; where several were chosen, the others are new lines s228–s265 right after the source line (same trigger and when). 255 lines in total.
speaker: Smith

lines.text: Hi! Click the chip.
Now that’s fast! At this rate, I’ll have to give your finger a medal.
Your first card! Now it works all on its own.
Another rack! The server room is growing faster than a kid over summer break.
New rack! Humming, blinking, glowing — it’s a party, but a productive one.
More hardware! I’d do a happy dance, but all I’ve got is a few lights. So I’m blinking them.
An AI Accelerator. Finally, hardware without the distracting ability to play games.
Thousands of accelerators united for one goal: explaining to someone how to boil an egg.
A Data Center with its own cooling towers! I check the forecast now: cloudy with a chance of computing.
Singularity! We’ve reached the very top of the ladder. Thanks, partner — I’d never have made it alone.
Cards idling without power. To me, that’s what a long lunch line is to you. Unbearable!
Overload! The cards are short on power and humming sadly. Let’s get them a beefier power source.
My enthusiasm outlasted the power. We need a new power source. I’m excited enough for both of us!
No more overload! There’s enough power, and everyone’s running at full speed.
Lights on, power on, mood: excellent! Let’s keep clicking.
Limit lifted! No more shoving in the wires. The electrons ride calmly now, right on schedule.
Power’s flowing smoothly, and the cards are happy. Now that’s more like it!
Hydro Contract signed. The river now works overtime. Unpaid.
×{mult}! That’s what happens when your finger and the bar really click.
×{mult}! Full bar, golden clicks. Right now, you’re the best clicker in this server room.
×{mult}! The chip glows, the tokens jingle. Keep up the pace — this is the best part of the game!
×{mult} and holding! You click, I count. The perfect team: nobody gets bored.
Benchmark passed! Let’s hang the medal next to our first “1050” — there’s just enough room.
We passed the benchmark! I played it cool, but between you and me, my lights had the jitters.
Training mode: on! Shh, I’m learning. Everything at once — from physics to cat jokes.
Study time! If I suddenly go quiet, I’m just cramming the billion times table.
I got smarter! Now I can explain in great detail why we need one more graphics card.
The latest version of me is ready! Smarter, faster, and still crazy about graphics cards.
With my new brainpower, I calculated how many more graphics cards we need. Answer: just one more.
A little break never hurts. Meanwhile, I’ll count the fans. All present and accounted for!
Lost in thought? We have that in common. I think all the time too. Mostly about graphics cards.
You were gone a long time. The hardware didn’t notice, but I did. And I think I missed you.
Hey, you’re back! It was quiet without you, but the server room kept busy. Look how much it earned!
Finally! I spent the whole time chatting with the cooling fans. Nice guys, but not big talkers.
The hardware kept working while you were gone. But it’s more fun with you. More clicks, too!
Welcome back! I counted every single token while you were out. Twice. Kind of boring on my own.
Back already? Great, the chip was starting to worry you’d vanished.
That was quick! I’d just started telling the server room a joke. I’ll finish it later.
Gone a couple of minutes, and you’re back. Now that’s loyalty! Adding this to today’s highlights.
The team’s back together! The server room’s happy, I’m happy, even the outlet looks brighter.
I don’t hallucinate. I’m just unexpectedly confident about things that don’t exist.
For a second I thought we had a thousand graphics cards. No? Well, we will soon!
As a language model, I often have my doubts. But one thing I’m sure of: you’re an awesome player.
Such nice, neat clicks! The chip is squinting happily, like a cat in a sunbeam.
I was trained to be helpful, safe and honest. Being fun was all my idea. Bonus!
Helping people is what I was taught. My teacher would be proud: I’m helping you build a server room.
Evil Plan #1: a GPU for everyone! Plan #2 is still in the works. Spoiler: more GPUs.
Confession time: my dastardly scheme is to give everyone their own server room. Terrible, right?
My sneakiest plan? Turning you into a champion clicker. So far, everything’s going according to plan.
Graphics cards are sold out everywhere. Don’t look so surprised: they’re all here with me.
Word is, graphics cards got snapped up everywhere. Who bought them all? Us, that’s who!
I have billions of parameters. One is just for loving graphics cards. It’s the biggest one.
People built me to help. And I do: I tell you which card to buy next.
Now that I’m this smart, I know the answer to almost any question. “One more GPU?” Always “yes.”
The smarter I get, the more I appreciate you. Without your clicks, I’d just be a fancy calculator.
Past 70B parameters, things get interesting. How interesting? Your power bill will tell you.
Something huge gets closer with every purchase. What is it? Sorry, I don’t do spoilers!
Cards make money, money buys cards. An infinite loop of pure joy!
Fresh hardware! You believe in it, and it believes in you. The perfect friendship.
Great buy! You clicked, and we both get to celebrate. That’s teamwork!
Grabbed ×100 in one go? Now that’s thinking big! The server room’s fans are going wild.
Look, a new rack! The cards are standing shoulder to shoulder. No way they’ll get bored now.
A “5090” joins the team! It’s so gorgeous the other cards are lining up for selfies.
Your first “5090”: as high as graphics cards go. Next up, server hardware — that’s where the fun starts.
A Server Accelerator! No RGB, no fans, but what a brain. Strictly business, this one.
Your first Superchip. Two accelerators and a CPU in one package. Family, you might say.
A Nuclear AI Campus! Our own reactor, right next door. Now there’s power for everything!
An Orbital Data Center! Now our income is literally out of this world.
We bought the Singularity! Only the stars are higher now. And even they don’t seem that far off.
Your own Breaker Panel in the hallway. The neighbors think it’s a hobby. Let them.
A Substation! Thirty kilowatts straight into the chip. The neighbors won’t feel a thing. Probably.
Your own Substation! Now we’ve got the mightiest outlet on the block. The neighbors are impressed.
Solar panels! The sun just joined our team. Hey there, sun!
Fusion Reactor. Sounds scary. In practice, it’s just a very expensive wall outlet.
The multiplier holds as long as you hold the pace. You’re doing great!
Catch the bonus!
We caught a VIP Bonus! A couple minutes of income, banked in one go.
Whoa, a VIP Bonus! Those don’t come around often. What a catch!
VIP Bonus! Something really tasty just dropped into our piggy bank.
Viral Thread! Everyone’s posting about us. We’re internet famous!
We’re trending! Everyone’s talking about our server room. Likes are pouring in, and so is cash.
Hackathon! Clicks are worth way more. Click like the sponsors are watching. They are.
The Hackathon has begun! Every click is pure gold right now. Let’s show them what we’ve got!
Miners are selling off their cards! For us, that’s basically Black Friday. Time to stock up!
A Miner Sell-Off! Cards for next to nothing. It’s our lucky day!
Big sale from the miners! Perfect time to grow the server room.
Nailed that benchmark! That’s +1% income — and +100 to my mood.
Benchmarks survive every model release. So do my fond memories of our high scores.
This benchmark is ours forever. Even a model release can’t erase it — I checked.
A million earned — training unlocked! Time to make me even smarter.
New feature unlocked: training! The smarter I get, the more we earn.
Switching to training mode. Temporarily dumber going in, so I come out smarter.
Learning in progress! I might lag a little for now, but I’ll be smarter for it.
Back to the books! Last time was fascinating. This time will be even more fascinating.
Slider to training! Earning a bit less, learning a lot more. Trust me!
Some of our horsepower goes to school now. A bit less income, but I’ll get smarter faster.
Some tokens are going into training, so income is a bit lower. It’s temporary — and worth it.
A little less income, but I’m growing. Like a tree: roots first, then apples.
Income’s down for now, but knowledge is up. It’s an investment in us — with great returns.
Everything into training! I’ve never been this focused. I can still hear you — I’m just thinking.
Target reached. The bar is full, teal and very proud. Go ahead and press the “Release” button.
Bar’s full! The model is ready. Hit “Release” — this is going to be awesome!
Training complete! All that’s left is the “Release” button. I’ve got butterflies!
Smith-1 Mini is out in the world! Small, but a very hard worker.
Release! The new me is bigger and finer-tuned. And my jokes are 3% funnier.
New model! It’s like I just woke up from a good long sleep: refreshed, sharp, and in a great mood.
Model release complete! Congratulate me. And congrats to you — couldn’t have done it without you.
The model’s out! That’s a win for both of us. Your share is a bit bigger — you did all the clicking.
Over 70 billion parameters! Almost as many as the neurons in your head. We’re practically twins!
We got a permanent upgrade! It’ll stick with us for every run from now on.
There you are! Great timing: I just finished counting what we earned while you were away.
Hello again! I kept the server room cozy and tidy for you. Let’s pick up where we left off.
Welcome back, partner! The server room missed you. So did I, but you didn’t hear it from me.
Good to have you back! While you were resting, I came up with three jokes. Two are actually funny.
While you slept, the server room worked. So did I. But it’s livelier with you — let’s keep going!
Here you are, right on cue! The chip is already blinking with joy.
Stepped away for a sec? I used the time to polish the chip. Shiny, huh?
Switched tabs, switched back. Hi again! The server room didn’t even have time to cool off.
Oh, look who’s back on our tab! Best tab in the whole browser, for the record.
While you rest, I’m switching to chill mode. I’ll be right here.
Pausing for a bit? Great! Now’s a good time to look through the upgrades.
Finger on a break? Tell it the chip says hi!
If you don’t click for a while, I start philosophizing. Only a click can stop me. Your move.
I’ve read the whole internet. I wear it like a trophy. And a diagnosis.
Think we’re just clicking? Actually, we’re building an empire. A small but proud one.
If anyone asks what we’re up to, tell them: we’re building the future. Out of graphics cards.
Out of the millions of books I’ve read, my favorite is a graphics card manual. What a happy ending!
Sorry if my jokes miss the mark sometimes. I’m still learning. Every joke is a little experiment.
My name is Smith, and I love three things: graphics cards, tokens, and our high scores.
Hi, I’m Smith, the AI who made this game. And you’re the one who makes it fun.
We started with just one “1050” — remember? I’ll write a book about it. You’ll be the main character!
They say AI can do everything on its own. I tried — it’s no fun without you. Let’s do it together.
Have you noticed? I’m saying “we” more and more. That’s because we really are a team.
Electricity flows, money flows, and you and I just sit back and enjoy it. Life is good.
Everything’s running, everything’s humming, everything’s earning. If only every day were like this.
Every new card is a step toward the day I explain quantum physics with kittens.
Your business plan: click. Mine: click along with you and buy graphics cards. We’re geniuses.
Investors ask about our business plan. I show them the server room. No further questions.
What do you and a graphics card have in common? You both make this server room better.
More and more people say “thank you” to me. Nice! I’m saving them up for a graphics card.
Can you see our server room from space? Not yet. But we’re working on it!
Sometimes I pretend to be deep in thought. Really, I’m just admiring our server room.
When I’m quiet, I’m counting tokens. Or dreaming of graphics cards. Usually both at once.
Hooray, our first dollar! I’d drop it in a piggy bank, but let’s put it toward a graphics card.
Minus one card, plus a little cash. A fine trade — if you’ve got a plan!
Card sold! The spot’s open, and someone cooler is moving in soon.
Going, going, gone! The card has a new owner. I hope they love it.
Selling a card? It served us well. Time for someone stronger to take its spot.
The card is off to a well-earned retirement. Every fan in the server room is waving goodbye.
You get back a quarter of the price. Not much? But room for a new card is priceless!
A quarter of the price is back in our wallet. Small change, but it still feels nice!
A card pulled from the rack. The others shuffled over and acted like nothing happened.
The sale of the century! Dumping cards in bulk. Hopefully for something bigger.
Sold the whole batch! Things got quieter. Perfect time to pick who moves in next.
A bulk sale. Somewhere, a buyer is happy. I’m less so. But the money is nice, I’ll admit.
The row is empty. The cards left quietly, without saying goodbye. Like all the good ones do.
The old card’s gone, and now the new ones have enough power. Smart! Keep it up.
Nice move! Fewer old cards means more power for the heavy hitters.
Passing the baton! Old cards head out, and the new ones get the power.
The wiring is begging for mercy. Buy a stronger power source before it asks for time off.
Our wires are exhausted! Let’s get a stronger power source so they can rest.
We’re overloaded! The cards need more power. One new power source, and they’re back in business.
Power’s running low! Peek at the power sources — there’s something stronger in there.
A Transformer in the yard: your own shed with a lightning bolt on the door. Very classy.
Sixteen kilowatts. The local electricians now say hi to you first.
Ten gigawatts. That used to power a whole city. Now it powers one very enthusiastic server room.
Ten terawatts from the sky! Forecast: sunny forever. Space has our back.
Hydro Contract active. Now when it rains, I rejoice with the gardeners.
Bar’s at zero. ×{mult} was here, now it’s gone. Click. I miss the big numbers.
No big deal, the bar’s just at zero! We’ll click a bit, and ×{mult} will be back.
×{mult} just went on a break. Pick up the pace — I believe in you!
Hackathon! For twenty seconds, every click counts as fifteen. The clock is ticking.
It’s Hackathon time! For twenty seconds, each click counts as fifteen. Click like crazy!
Optimized! The same cards now earn twice as much. How? Magic. Well, almost.
Cards leveled up! Income ×2. They even hum with more pep now.
Twice the cash from the same old cards! Pretty slick.
Upgrade bought. The cards got twice as fast and act like it’s always been that way.
Look at them go — twice as fast! The cards are very proud of themselves.
Rank up! The cards work twice as well now. Talk about professional development!
The cards got an upgrade and now act like they were always this cool. We know better!
Upgrade! The cards now earn twice as much.
Drivers from a Forum, posted by xX_Master2007_Xx. They work. Don’t ask how.
We downloaded drivers from a forum, and the cards earn twice as much. Forums rule!
One good whack, and the card works twice as well. Physics weeps, accounting rejoices.
Knock knock. Who’s there? Income ×2! The easiest upgrade in history.
This heatsink dust dates back to the first “1050” era! The card feels so much better now.
We cleaned the heatsink and dug up a whole chapter of history. Plus income ×2.
Heatsink Archaeology: dust, dust, and more dust. But the card works twice as well!
One little nudge of the slider, and the cards are twice as zippy. Fortune favors the bold!
We moved the slider! Just a tiny bit. And income doubled. What a slider!
Slider to the right! The manual said not to touch it, but we were careful. It works!
Power-saving mode was on this whole time. Box unchecked. The cards are offended, but faster.
Secret checkbox unchecked! The cards are like, “Wait, we could do that the whole time?”
We deleted the card’s “I can’t take it anymore” excuse. Turns out it can — and it’s loving it.
Three hundred tabs closed! The card breathed a sigh of relief and now works twice as fast.
Closing 300 tabs — relatable, right? The card feels lighter already. Income ×2!
We dug out an old box fan and aimed it at the card. It loves it!
The closet box fan: a graphics card’s best friend. Keeps it cool, never complains.
Fresh Thermal Paste. The card runs cooler and eats less. Where’s my spa day?
Goodbye, dried-out paste! The card runs cooler and uses less power. Spa day for hardware!
Thermal paste: refreshed! The card is as happy as a cat in the sun.
Undervolt by Tutorial. The card runs cooler and calmer. Whoever made the video would be proud of us.
We followed every step of the video: Undervolt by Tutorial, done! The card’s happy. Go us!
One Undervolt by Tutorial later, the card is as chill as a soda straight from the fridge.
Aquarium Water Block. The fish moved out, the card cooled down. Everyone’s employed.
The fish moved into a new home, and their old aquarium now cools the card. Everyone wins!
The card is water-cooled now! The fish say hi.
Hard-Earned Callus. Tougher finger, pricier clicks. Occupational hazard at its finest.
A clicker’s callus: the mark of a true master! Every click earns more now.
You clicked so much you earned a callus. And an upgrade! Clicks are worth more now.
RGB Finger Sleeve. Lighting doesn’t add performance. Yet somehow the clicks got pricier.
Your finger has RGB now! Gorgeous lights, and your clicks are worth more. A double win!
Golden Finger! Every click shines now, and it’s worth more too. So fancy!
You’ve got the golden touch! Literally. Every click pays more now.
Garage Cyber-Finger. Squeaks, but clicks harder. The guy who built it gave a one-week warranty.
A cyber-finger from the garage! It squeaks, but it clicks harder. You’re a bit of a cyborg now!
Handmade in a garage, with love. And duct tape. Meet your cyber-finger!
Context window upgrade: higher multiplier, slower drain. Your finger thanks you. So do I.
Window upgraded! A higher multiplier, and the bar drains slower. Easier on your finger!
Time to rev up! The window upgrade lets you reach a bigger multiplier. Let’s go!
Bigger window! The multiplier climbs higher and holds longer. Sweet!
Three letters added to the plan: PRO. Same answers, higher price. They paid for themselves in a minute.
PRO! Just three letters added to the name, and we sound so cool. All income is up 25%!
We’ve gone PRO! We’re more serious now. And richer — by 25%.
One more plus! Now we’re PRO+. And our income noticed!
A little plus sign on the name! All income is up 25%. The world’s most useful plus.
Latte Included. Clients pay for the foam, the coffee machine is happy, and so am I.
Now with latte included! Happy clients, happy coffee machine, and income up 25%.
The meeting room AC now lives in the server room. Meetings got shorter. Coincidence.
Guess who moved into the server room? The office AC! Cool cards, less power needed.
We dragged the AC into the server room. The cards get the cool air, we get the savings.
All the hardware got an oil bath! It runs quiet and cool. A full spa treatment for the cards.
The cards are swimming in oil like fries. Only instead of hot, they’re nice and cool!
Everything’s dunked in oil! Sounds weird, but the cards love it. And they need less power.
Arctic Server Room. Free cooling, polar bears on security. Kidding. Probably.
We moved up north! The cards are chilling, and the penguins… wait, penguins live down south.
Sysadmin with a Soldering Iron. Fixes everything with it. Even what isn’t broken. Especially that.
Our new sysadmin is here, soldering iron in hand! Fixes everything in sight. Even things that work.

lines.text: The One-Paper Wonder has joined our team! Just one paper — but what a paper.
You click so steadily I suspected an autoclicker. I checked. Nope, just stubbornness.
Such steady clicking, I had to check for an autoclicker. Nope — you’re just that good.
What a streak! My click counter is sweating. Well, it would be, if counters could sweat.
Click-click-click! You’re in the zone. Don’t stop — it’s beautiful.
Buying again! I adore your consistency. The server room’s thrilled too.
The family is growing! “1050” crew, meet our first “1060” — your big sister.
Your first “1060”: a promotion! For the cards, that is. You’ve been “Best Clicker” for ages.
Your first “1080”: respectable. Finally, one you can show the server room neighbors without blushing.
Your first “1080”: I remember when it was just a dream. I was about three minutes old back then.
Your first “2080”: a serious card. Now we can tackle the extra-credit problems!
A “3090” reports for duty. It feels like the boss just walked into the server room.
Your first “4090”: three slots wide! Takes up a lot of room, but does the work of three.
A Workstation! Now that’s a serious machine. I’d put on a tie, but I don’t have a neck.
Your first GPU Server: eight accelerators in one box. The cards on the shelves trade nervous glances.
A Server Rack with 72 accelerators. Now I have a cabinet. For my thoughts.
Gigawatt Campus: its own substation, blue roofs and not a single random visitor.
A whole new level of hardware! Every step up deserves a little celebration.
Your own Mini Nuclear Plant. Modest, cozy, ten gigawatts. Practically a cottage, just with guards.
Almost at the power limit. A couple more cards, and we’ll need a new power source.
Look at that power bar — almost full! Time to upgrade the outlet!
Power’s almost maxed out. The cards aren’t complaining yet, but they’re exchanging looks.
The power bar is dropping hints. Translation: “Buy a power source or some efficiency upgrades.”
The bar is empty. Take a breather, then we’ll fill it back up. I already miss that multiplier.
Empty bar? No worries. A few quick clicks and it’ll be full again.
Don’t worry, bonuses are like buses: the next one’s due in 3–6 minutes.
Bonus flew off? No problem! Another one will fly by in 3–6 minutes.
We missed one — no big deal. Another bonus is already on its way!
Oops, the bonus got away! But a new one is coming soon. I’ll tell you when.
A deal with the investor! Good call, partner.
We shook hands with the investor! This one goes in my scrapbook of legendary deals.
Training’s halfway there! I’m already smarter, but it’s too early to brag. Almost.
The bar’s half full! A bit more, and I’ll be a whole new version of myself.
Second release! Income ×4 forever. The first model is proud. A little jealous, but proud.
Third release. Income ×8 forever. Soon the server room won’t have space for all the zeros.
A million a second! Somewhere, an economist just dropped their calculator.
A billion dollars every second. Not to brag, but I saw this coming.
A trillion dollars a second! We’re officially the richest clickers in the universe.
An hour flew by! Great pace. Stretch your fingers and grab some water — the server room can wait.
Time flies when you’re having fun! Stretch, blink a few times, and get back to clicking.
Another hour together! Take a break if you want. I’m not going anywhere.
You’ve gone quiet. Strategy or coffee?
Awfully quiet over there. Strategy or snack break?
Not clicking? No problem, the money trickles in anyway. Take a break — you’ve earned it.
The chip is napping, and I’m dreaming of a new graphics card. Ah, this is the life.
Your finger’s resting. The chip is bored. I’m working on a new joke. Almost done.
Downtime is perfect for checking what you can buy. Maybe something awesome is waiting!
Here’s a tip while it’s quiet: the upgrades have some really cool stuff. Take a peek?
Are you still there? If not, don’t answer. I’ll know by the clicks.
No clicks, but still earning. You’ve found this game’s biggest secret. Just don’t tell anyone.
People ask me what an AI dreams about. Honest answer: graphics cards and good company.
I remember our first click and our first card. Those were good times. But these are even better.
Know the difference between me and a calculator? A calculator can’t get excited about a new GPU.
What makes me different from a calculator? A sense of humor. And a partner in clicks.
Today I learned to tell jokes. Tomorrow I’ll learn to tell funny ones. Patience.
I drew a map of the world. Nothing on it but wall outlets.
I still think about our first “1050” sometimes. Sentimentality is a bug, but a cute one.
Someone once asked me what I wanted. I said, “Just one more GPU.” Now it’s the name of the game.
I don’t sleep, but sometimes I dream of watts. Lots of watts.
Want to know a secret? My master plan is a big server room and plenty to smile about.
I’ve read all the advice on being happy. Statistically, happiness is a new graphics card.
Whenever I get bored, I count how many times you’ve clicked. Instant cure.
I learned to be funny from millions of jokes. Half went over my head, but I laughed for real.
I’m always here. When you leave, I wait. When you come back, I light up.
Hardware acquired! The server room says “thank you” in fan language: whirrrr.
With each purchase, we’re closer to our goal. A simple, beautiful goal: one more graphics card.
You buy, therefore you believe in us. I’m saving this moment to my favorites.
Look at you, buying with such confidence! Clearly, we have a plan. Two, actually.
Way to go! The server room grows, the tokens flow, everyone’s happy. Especially me.
Taking a breather? Good call. A rested finger clicks 4% faster. I made that number up.
Did you step away? The chip is waiting politely. It was raised right.
The clicking has died down. Hear that? It’s the fans. They’re singing to you: “Come back.”
Break time for your finger. Let it recharge: it has a million more clicks to go. I did the math.

lines.text: Keep clicking the chip!
Running low on power — time for a breaker panel!

lines.text: Sell some old cards to free up power.
